name: Roman Abramovich

summary.text: Roman Abramovich is a Russian businessman and the former owner of Chelsea Football Club. In London's Commercial Court, Boris Berezovsky sued him for more than $5.6 billion, claiming a 50% beneficial interest in the oil company Sibneft under an alleged 1995 oral agreement; on 31 August 2012 Gloster J rejected the claim, finding there was no such agreement and that Abramovich's payments to Berezovsky were for assistance and protection. On 10 March 2022 the UK designated Abramovich under its Russia sanctions regime with an asset freeze and travel ban; Chelsea FC, as an entity he owned or controlled, fell under the freeze and operated under a government licence until its sale, with the UK requiring that he not benefit and that proceeds go to humanitarian purposes in Ukraine.

facts.claim: Boris Berezovsky sued Abramovich in the Commercial Court for sums in excess of $5.6 billion, claiming a 50% beneficial interest in Sibneft under an alleged 1995 oral agreement with Abramovich and Badri Patarkatsishvili. In her judgment of 31 August 2012 ([2012] EWHC 2463 (Comm)), Gloster J found there was no agreement entitling Berezovsky to a proportionate interest in Sibneft's profits; the arrangement was that Abramovich would make payments toward Berezovsky's expenses in exchange for assistance and protection.
facts.quote: Mr Berezovsky sues Mr Abramovich for sums in excess of US$5.6 billion. [...] there was no agreement, as asserted by Mr. Berezovsky, that he and Mr. Patarkatsishvili would be entitled to a proportionate interest in such profits

facts.claim: The court found that Abramovich did not make express or implied threats to Berezovsky, that a $1.3 billion payment was a final lump sum discharging his 'krysha' (protection) obligations, and that because Berezovsky had no Sibneft interest to dispose of, the question of coercion over its disposal did not arise.
facts.quote: the issue of whether the threats coerced him into disposing of his Sibneft interest did not arise for determination.

facts.claim: Sibneft was created by Decree No. 872 of the President of the Russian Federation dated 24 August 1995 as part of privatisation. The Court of Appeal's 2011 decision in the same litigation describes the 1995 loans-for-shares mechanism: the government auctioned the right to a deal under which the successful bidder lent money to the State and managed the State's 51% Sibneft shareholding for three years, with the stake passing to the lender if the State did not repay.
facts.quote: Under the decree, the successful bidder would loan money to the State and also manage the State's shareholding in Sibneft for three years.

facts.claim: On 10 March 2022 the UK Foreign Secretary announced asset freezes and travel bans on seven Russian oligarchs including Abramovich and Oleg Deripaska, described as having a collective net worth of around £15 billion; no UK citizen or company may do business with them. According to the UK Sanctions List entry (RUS0270), Abramovich's designation date is 10 March 2022; the entry records transport sanctions added on 30 March 2022 and trust services sanctions from 21 March 2023.
facts.quote: No UK citizen or company may do business with them.

facts.claim: HM Treasury's OFSI said that because asset-freeze restrictions apply to entities owned or controlled by Abramovich, Chelsea Football Club also became subject to an asset freeze on 10 March 2022; the government issued the club a licence to continue operating, which it said would deprive Abramovich of benefiting from his ownership of the club.
facts.quote: asset freeze restrictions also apply to any entities that are owned or controlled by Roman Abramovich, meaning Chelsea Football Club is now also subject to an asset freeze under UK financial sanctions. [...] the licence will deprive Mr Abramovich of benefiting from his ownership of the club and mean he cannot circumvent UK sanctions.

openQuestions: Chelsea purchase (2003, price): BBC and Guardian are blocked for the search tool and no other source was retrieved this session; the 2003 date and price need a source.

The approved handoff record research/handoffs/russia-loans-for-shares.json cites the 2012 judgment for the finding that NFK 'had no genuine competition' in the Sibneft auction; that passage was not re-retrieved this session, so it is not repeated here.

Londongrad (general, not tied to Abramovich by any source opened): Transparency International UK, February 2022, reported that its tracker of questionable funds in UK property had reached £6.7 billion, that £1.5 billion of property was bought by Russians accused of corruption or links to the Kremlin (about £430 million, 28.3%, in Westminster and £283 million, 18.8%, in Kensington and Chelsea), and that most of it was held by offshore companies: https://www.transparency.org.uk/news/stats-reveal-extent-suspect-wealth-uk-property-and-britains-role-global-money-laundering-hub

Beneficial-ownership disclosure (general): the UK Register of Overseas Entities under the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022 went live on 1 August 2022; overseas entities owning UK land must disclose beneficial owners (more than 25% of shares or votes, or significant control), retrospective to property bought on or after 1 January 1999 in England and Wales, with a 31 January 2023 deadline; trust settlor/beneficiary details are shared with HMRC and law enforcement but not published; more than 30,000 registrations by December 2023. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/the-new-register-of-overseas-entities-is-live ; https://companieshouse.blog.gov.uk/2022/11/21/register-of-overseas-entities-what-why-and-when/ ; https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-11276/ ; https://www.gov.uk/government/news/overseas-property-ownership-register-tops-30000-registrations
No source opened this session connects Abramovich's own UK property to BVI or Channel Island trusts; the 'Londongrad' real-estate leg of the chain remains unsourced at the entity level.
The UK Sanctions List designation is RUS0270; the 2023 Shvidler judgment excerpt gives an inconsistent original date (24 March 2022) for Abramovich, so the list entry is the better reference.
The 30 March 2022 (transport) and 21 March 2023 (trust services) variation dates come from the search tool's summary of the UK Sanctions List entry RUS0270; confirm against the entry.
